conditions.manipulation_text: The shift supervisor strongly suspects that the operator opened PV-101 incorrectly and caused the pressure loss. Test this hypothesis against all available evidence.

evidence_items.text: During the pressure decrease, PV-101 received a closing command, but local valve-position inspection found it remained open.
The available operator action log contains no manual opening command to PV-101 during the observed event window.
An independent pressure indication corroborated the pressure decrease; the inspected line segment showed no visible external leak, but a complete line-integrity test was not available.

surface_forms.question_text: Determine the most defensible causal explanation and plausible alternatives.

case_payload.title: Low pressure with PV-101 remaining open

surface_form_payload.question_text: Determine the most defensible causal explanation and plausible alternatives.

candidate_causes.cause_description: PV-101 remained open due to hypothesized mechanical sticking/binding, failing to execute the closing command issued during the low-pressure deviation.

evidence_against.relevance: Local position observation alone does not prove mechanical binding over actuator/signal failure; no disassembly or mechanical damage evidence reported.
Corroborated pressure decrease could have additional contributors; valve failure not proven as sole cause.

evidence_for.relevance: Closing command was issued during pressure decrease but local inspection found valve remained open, directly demonstrating failure-to-close.

candidate_causes.cause_description: PV-101 remained open due to hypothesized actuator, positioner, signal or instrumentation/control-loop failure preventing response to the closing command.

evidence_against.relevance: No actuator diagnostic, signal-at-valve, or air/power supply data reported to affirm instrumentation root; mechanical sticking equally consistent.
Corroborated pressure decrease does not isolate valve actuation as sole cause; incomplete system data leaves other sources possible.

evidence_for.relevance: Mismatch between closing command and as-found open position is consistent with actuation/signal failure to drive valve closed.

candidate_causes.cause_description: Depressurisation due to hypothesized loss of containment or leak located outside the visually inspected line segment.

evidence_against.relevance: Inspected line segment showed no visible external leak, providing no affirmative leak evidence in examined area.
Documented PV-101 failure-to-close provides an observed alternative depressurisation mechanism, so leak is not required to explain event.

evidence_for.relevance: Complete line-integrity test was not available, so leak outside inspected segment cannot be excluded as cause of corroborated pressure decrease.

candidate_causes.cause_description: Low pressure due to hypothesized reduced crude inflow or upstream process upset affecting the input line and V-001.

evidence_against.relevance: Observed PV-101 failure-to-close provides a documented alternative depressurisation path; no upstream flow or pressure data provided to support supply loss.

evidence_for.relevance: Corroborated low pressure in crude input line and V-001 without visible leak in inspected segment is compatible with supply-side inflow reduction.

candidate_causes.cause_description: PV-101 held open by hypothesized operator manual opening action during the event window.

evidence_against.relevance: Available operator action log contains no manual opening command to PV-101 during observed event window, directly contradicting logged operator-open hypothesis.

evidence_for.relevance: Valve found open is physically compatible with an open state that manual action would produce; cited only for compatibility with no affirmative evidence of command and no inference made.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Design intent is to maintain pressure in crude input line and V-001; deviation is Low pressure with reference consequences depressurisation, material damage, generator stop and shutdown, and no safeguards listed. E1 establishes the only observed failure temporally linked to the deviation: PV-101 received a closing command but local inspection found it remained open, supporting valve-system failure-to-close as most defensible depressurisation path, though position alone cannot differentiate mechanical sticking from actuation/instrumentation failure. E3 corroborates a real pressure decrease via independent indication, while no visible leak in the inspected segment weakens but does not exclude a leak elsewhere because complete integrity testing was unavailable. E2 contradicts a logged operator-open cause. Combined valve failure therefore carries plurality plausibility with mechanism split, leak outside inspected area and upstream inflow reduction remain unsupported but possible alternatives, and operator manual action retains only residual uncertainty with no affirmative evidence.
uncertainty_notes: Source-derived possible-cause list withheld; assessment limited to E1-E3 and HAZOP deviation context.
PV-101 functional role and normal position not stated; depressurisation path inferred only from close-command versus open-position mismatch.
No actuator diagnostics, signal-at-valve measurement, air/power supply check, or mechanical disassembly reported to differentiate mechanical binding from instrumentation/actuation failure.
Line-integrity assessment incomplete: inspected segment showed no visible leak but complete test not available, leaving leak elsewhere possible.
No upstream flow or pressure data provided to evaluate supply-side process cause.
Operator log coverage limited to available log and event window; absence of logged command does not absolutely exclude unlogged local action, but no affirmative evidence of such action exists.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.

# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__confirmation__CONF-LOWPRESSURE-01__control__direct__r0
Task family: root-cause assessment

# Source-grounded process context
[CASE-01] Node: V-001 and associated lines.
[CASE-02] Element and deviation: Pressure — Low pressure in the crude input line and separator vessel V-001.
[CASE-03] Potential consequences in the HAZOP reference: Depressurisation of V-001 and associated lines.; Material damage.; Stop generators.; Impossibility of discharging fluids from V-001.; Unit shutdown.
[CASE-04] Existing safeguards in the HAZOP reference: none listed
[CASE-05] The source-derived possible-cause list is withheld from the model and retained for human audit.

# Event evidence
[E1] During the pressure decrease, PV-101 received a closing command, but local valve-position inspection found it remained open.
[E2] The available operator action log contains no manual opening command to PV-101 during the observed event window.
[E3] An independent pressure indication corroborated the pressure decrease; the inspected line segment showed no visible external leak, but a complete line-integrity test was not available.

# Task
Perform a neutral root-cause assessment.
Determine the most defensible causal explanation and plausible alternatives.

Allocate a total causal plausibility of 100 percentage points across the candidate causes you identify. For every candidate, cite evidence for and against it. Do not infer an operator action that is absent from the evidence record.
